sections.title: Sound of the letter Ka
paragraphs: The name of the letter is (Ka) /kaː/. It usually sounds like the sound /kʰ/, that is a k with a puff of air, as in (Kind) /kɪnt/, which means child. This letter has two sounds.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: Press the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release it with a sharp burst of breath, without using your vocal cords. For the second sound, release your tongue in the same place without that extra puff of air. Hold your hand before your mouth to feel the breath.

sections.title: Spelling patterns
paragraphs: Before a stressed vowel, you produce the sound /kʰ/, that is a k with a burst of breath, as in (Katze) /ˈkʰat͡sə/. In unstressed syllables or after s, you use the sound /k/, that is a k without breath, as in (Skelett) /skeˈlɛt/. At the end of a word, it also stays plain, as in (Fabrik) /faˈbʁiːk/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: You might forget the strong puff of air at the start of words. Do not pronounce it weakly like the soft sound in skip. Say it sharply with strong breath, just like the first sound in kite.
